title: introduce-tenant-policy-signer-and-roster-auditor
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: customers running Private deployments and Dedicated tenants ask for cryptographically verifiable RBAC policy rollouts and a way to detect drift between declared tenant policies and what is actually enforced by the runtime. This PR implements a tenant policy snapshot signer, a roster-based RBAC auditor that reconciles declared role mappings with live bindings, and wiring to surface policy signatures in audit logs for post-hoc verification.

What this does (high level):
- policy-signer service: generates signed snapshots (rbac-v2.1 snapshot format) for tenant policy manifests. Uses customer KMS or a cluster HSM key (via KMS envelope) to sign a compact snapshot and stores metadata in /policies/snapshots. Signatures are detached and included in the snapshot metadata so any party with the public verification key can verify integrity.
- roster-auditor CLI: pulls declared snapshots and compares against live RBAC bindings in the authz store (and cloud provider IAM mappings for Dedicated). Runs in dry-run/advisory mode by default; implements --enforce for operator use. Produces a reconciliation report and emits audit events when drift is detected.
- audit enrichment: attach header X-Policy-Snapshot-Signature to policy-change audit events and include snapshot_id in audit payloads. Console shows Signed snapshot timeline under Team -> Policies.
- private-installer change: installer now optionally provisions a signer KMS key and bootstraps a verifier key into tenant metadata when in "signed-policies" mode.
- compliance hooks: added a reconcile schedule that can be enabled per-tenant and policies for how aggressive drift remediation alerts are.

Checklist: 
- [x] signer core implementation and API (generate/verify)
- [x] roster reconcile CLI and dry-run reports
- [x] console timeline and policy detail view
- [x] audit log enrichment header and schema bump
- [x] private-installer manifest wiring and integration test
- [x] end-to-end integration test using local KMS emulator

Commits (summary):
- add: internal/policy/signer: snapshot generation and signing using KMS envelope (key-wrapping + signing flow)
- add: internal/policy/verifier: public-key verification and snapshot fetcher with caching
- add: cmd/roster-auditor: reconcile CLI, report formatter, and reconciliation rules engine
- feat: api: /policies/snapshots endpoint, pagination and lookup by tenant+snapshot_id
- ui: console: policy timeline, signature verification status, and drift alerts panel
- infra: private-installer: optional signer key provisioning and tenant metadata bootstrap
- tests: integration/e2e: local-kms-emulator scenario and installer end-to-end test

Changed files (representative):
- internal/policy/signer.go
- internal/policy/verifier.go
- cmd/roster-auditor/main.go
- api/handlers/policy_snapshots.go
- console/src/pages/PolicyTimeline.tsx
- private-installer/templates/signer.yaml
- docs/security/policy_signing.md
- tests/e2e/policy_signing_test.go

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests added for signer/verifier and reconciliation rules.
- Integration suite runs against a KMS emulator in CI (flaky in one run; re-ran and passing).
- Load test smoke: signing latency measured ~9ms median on dev infra; verification on warm cache ~2ms.

Review notes and decisions:
- Signature format: chose detached compact signature (rbac-v2.1 snapshot + signature metadata) to avoid changing existing runtime policy loader format; runtime verifies signature optionally when tenant config requires enforcement.
- Advisory mode default: roster-auditor runs in dry-run to prevent accidental enforcement during rollout; operators must opt-in to --enforce. This was requested by Security to avoid surprise denials.
- KMS integration: supports AWS KMS, GCP KMS and on-prem HSM via existing KMS envelope abstraction. Installer offers a convenience flow for key provisioning; enterprise customers can supply their own keys.

Risks and mitigations:
- Key compromise: snapshots are signed but not encrypted; we added rotation guidance, revocation list handling in docs, and recommend short-lived verifier keys for high-assurance tenants.
- Backwards compatibility: runtimes that don't fetch verification still accept policy manifests; signature verification is opt-in. We added feature flag and gradual rollout via canary to Dedicated nodes.
- Operational complexity: added observability metrics (policy.signer.latency, policy.reconcile.drift_count) and runbooks in docs/security.

Release notes: 
- Added tenant policy snapshot signing and roster reconciliation tooling for RBAC v2.1. Operators can now generate verifiable policy snapshots and run automated audits to detect tenant policy drift. Audit logs include policy snapshot identifiers and signatures for downstream verification.

release_notes: Tenant policy snapshot signing and roster-based audit/reconcile tooling (rbac-v2.1). Includes console timeline, audit enrichment, and optional installer key provisioning.
notes_for_ops: To enable signed policy enforcement for a tenant: provision signer key via installer or bring-your-own, generate initial snapshot with policy-signer, configure tenant.enforce_signed_policies=true, and enable reconcile schedule if desired. See docs/security/policy_signing.md for runbooks.
manual_steps_after_merge: Run private-installer with --enable-signer for environments that will use signer keys; for existing tenants, generate initial snapshot and run roster-auditor --dry-run to preview drift before enabling enforcement.
